diagnostic_evidence.quote: On the other hand, for $n_0=0.25$, the policy related to $\J^2$ performs poorly since the mean TTP has more than halved if compared to the other treatment approaches.

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction states without qualification that the hyperbolic-cost policy outperforms MTD and AT on average in TTP, citing the two tables. Table Sum_Hyp gives a mean TTP' of 102 days for n0=0.25, against 210 days (MTD) and 213 days (On-Off AT). The paper itself later calls this 'performs poorly'. The claim holds only for n0=0.50 and 0.75. The hyperbolic rows also use TTP' while the benchmarks use TTP, and the min TTP' values collapse to 9 and 15 days.

failure_location.quote: and on average it outperforms MTD and AT in terms of `time to progression'

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the statement to n0 in {0.50, 0.75}, mention the failure at n0=0.25 and the collapse of min TTP', and note the TTP vs TTP' convention.
issues.overall_effect: The headline numerical conclusion is overstated and contradicted by the paper's own data for one of the three tested regimes.
issues.title: Introduction claims hyperbolic policy outperforms MTD/AT on average, contradicted by the n0=0.25 results
issues.why_classification: A local rewording of one sentence fixes it; no result, computation or guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we can deduce that the set $\Delta_1$ is invariant

issues.failure_explanation: On x1=0 the displayed dynamics is r'= r(\hat r_R(1-r)-\hat d_T). This is nonnegative iff r <= 1-\hat d_T/\hat r_R, not iff r <= \hat r_R/(\hat r_R+\hat d_T). The two thresholds agree only when \hat d_T=0, the case used in the experiments. For \hat d_T>0 the case split in the proof is false. The case split is only used to get 'r stays in [0,1]', which does hold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the threshold by 1-\hat d_T/\hat r_R (with the case where it is non-positive treated separately), or simply note that r'<=0 at r=1 and that r=0 is stationary.
issues.overall_effect: The stated sign analysis in the proof is incorrect for general \hat d_T>0, although the invariance of Delta_1 and the lemma's conclusion survive.
issues.title: Wrong sign threshold for the resistant-cell dynamics in the invariance proof
issues.why_classification: A one-line recomputation fixes the case split and the lemma and its uses remain intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: every $L^2$-weak limiting point of $(u^\star_N)_{N\geq1}$ is a minimizer for $\J$
which has a support consisting of $N=1225$ points

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is asymptotic. It concerns a sequence mu_N converging weak-* to mu, and says only that weak limit points of the minimizers u_N^* minimize J. It gives no statement, bound or rate for a single fixed N, and no quantitative statement that an arbitrary minimizer of J_N is near-optimal for J. The experiments use one fixed measure with N=1225 and only approximate (gradient-descent) minimizers. The paper's own tables show large worst-case discrepancies, e.g. min TTP' of 9 and 15 days.

failure_location.quote: \cref{thm:exist_Gamma} ensures that any minimizer of $\J_N$ is a good competitor as well for the original objective functional $\J$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the result as asymptotic (limit points of minimizers of J_N for mu_N weak-* converging to mu), and say that for the fixed N used the closeness to the J-problem is only heuristic, optionally checked by refining the grid.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical justification offered for using a single discretised measure in the numerical section is overstated. The optimality and robustness of the computed controls for the continuous ensemble is not guaranteed.
issues.title: Remark claims the Gamma-convergence theorem justifies any minimizer of a fixed discretised J_N
issues.why_classification: Rewording the remark to match the theorem suffices; theorem, algorithms and numerics are untouched.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which has a support consisting of $N=1225$ points

issues.failure_explanation: The grid {0.5,0.52,...,1} has 26 points and {0.002,0.004,...,0.1} has 50 points. Summing j=1..25 and k=1..49 with weights 1/25 and 1/49 cannot cover these grids. If all listed nodes carry those weights, the weights total (26/25)(50/49) and mu_N is not a probability measure. The stated N=1225 should be 1300 for the listed grid, and the text's [0.002,1] should read [0.002,0.1]. Which set of nodes and weights was actually used in the simulations is not determined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the grids as 26 and 50 nodes with weights 1/26 and 1/50 and N=1300 (or state the grid actually used), and confirm the tabulated statistics correspond to that measure.
issues.overall_effect: The ensemble measure used for every reported mean TTP and for the computed controls is ambiguously defined, so the numerical statistics cannot be reproduced exactly as stated.
issues.title: Discrete ensemble measure: node counts, weights and N inconsistent with the listed grid
issues.why_classification: A bookkeeping correction of counts and weights; the method and the qualitative conclusions are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the resolution of an ensemble optimal control problem tends automatically to find the interval where the decision-making on the therapy schedule has the most significant effect

issues.failure_explanation: The gradient is nabla_u J(tau) = int g(tau) F_1(x(tau)) dmu, with g(T)=0 and g' bounded. Hence |nabla_u J(tau)| = O(T-tau) for every T, every parameter set and every control, regardless of tumour dynamics. The cost on [tau,T] is a short integral when tau is near T. So the observed smallness of the gradient (and the controls staying near the initial guess 0.5 there) carries no information about whether T is large enough or whether late decisions matter. The proposed 'empirical test' is vacuous, and the justification of the arbitrary T in rmk:choice_T rests on it. The remark's opening sentence that the computed controls 'do not deviate significantly' from 0.5 also contradicts the later description of u^1 equal to 1 for about 400 days and u^2 equal to 0 initially.

failure_location.quote: We can use this phenomenon as an empirical test for deciding whether the time horizon $T$ has been appropriately set large

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the claim that gradient smallness validates T, and either say that T is a modelling choice or test sensitivity directly by re-solving with several horizons.
issues.overall_effect: The justification for the choice of the time horizons in Table Time_horizon and the assertion that the optimisation 'automatically' locates the relevant time interval are unsupported.
issues.title: Small gradient near T is forced by the terminal condition, so it cannot test the horizon choice
issues.why_classification: Only a methodological heuristic is affected; deleting or replacing it leaves all theorems and computed results intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Namely, we aim to formulate an adaptive therapy that allows tumor growth to be controlled at the early stage of the therapy, without exceeding the progression threshold.
However, as soon as the tumor size gets close to the progression threshold, the therapy is started.
The TTP of `On-Off'~AT and `Off-On'~AT is $424$ days and $459$ days, respectively, with a progression delay of $5$ weeks.

issues.failure_explanation: Under Off-On AT, therapy starts only after n >= 1.2 n0, which is exactly the progression event defined by tau_TTP. So the threshold is reached by construction, and 'without exceeding the progression threshold' and 'gets close to' are false. Moreover tau_TTP, as defined in eq:def_TTP, equals the end of the initial untreated phase, i.e. the free-growth time from n0 to 1.2 n0. For theta=(1.5,0,0.66,0.01), n0=0.5 this is about 15 days. Hence the 424/459-day TTPs and Table Off-On cannot be values of eq:def_TTP. They must be TTP' (last time below threshold), which is not stated for this table, although the paper insists on this switch for the Hyperbolic rows. Also, for n0=0.75 the maximum TTP of 1500 days equals the simulation horizon, so it is censored.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that Table Off-On reports TTP' and handle the horizon-censored values. Drop the claim of not exceeding the threshold, or change the trigger to a level below 1.2 n0 and re-run the experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed improvement of Off-On over On-Off AT, and the stated rationale of avoiding the progression threshold, are not supported as written. The metric used in Table Off-On is inconsistent with the defined TTP and is not disclosed.
issues.title: Off-On AT contradicts its stated aim and the TTP definition used to evaluate it
issues.why_classification: Fixing it needs a contained redefinition or re-evaluation of the metric, and possibly new simulations if the algorithm is changed, but the framework and the qualitative message survive.
